rulings.a: keep fuel L/100 km (logged/app-calculated) as the single confirmatory outcome; gross traction is computed from fuel flow x BSFC plus battery power minus auxiliaries (recon_engine.py), so it is not an independent, cleaner outcome; regeneration-to-battery (from logged current) stays exploratory with its own expectation
rulings.b: rejected as written: the reconstruction has no mass term, so scaling the mass-dependent terms is undefined and R1 at k=1 is trivially true; redefine B1 as a kinematic reference (positive KE throughput from logged speed, exactly proportional to m, plus rolling C_rr*m*g*d with C_rr in {0.008, 0.010, 0.012} as an assumed value) or drop it
rulings.c: 5 km floor accepted with 2 and 10 km sensitivities; displaced-day placebo as primary (payload from another day, same class, thermal class and month, distance-matched; placebo/primary ratio, threshold 0.5, interval, as in M768); the within-day permutation degenerates (one occupant set per trip day) and is only a diagnostic (share of days whose payload varies)
rulings.d: no: 'associated with', 'per 100 kg of estimated payload'; proxy error attenuates the slope, so a null is never 'no mass sensitivity' (no TOST)
rulings.e: yes, exploratory; use the four M753 classes (mixed_highway included); highway has about 20 drives with a pattern: counts only there

required_changes: physics: +3 to 4 % treats the mass share of gross traction as the fuel elasticity; regeneration recovery, auxiliaries, warm-up and idle are mass-independent, so the elasticity of a hybrid is about 0.2 to 0.6, i.e. +1 to +3 % per +100 kg; pre-register the bracket and put its LOWER end into the reading rule
add a design-based MDE sizing from the payload SD (39 kg) and the effective number of days before any outcome is read; likely outcome: not informative
A1 covariates: drop engine-on share (mediator); add net battery energy or dSOC per drive (buffer confound), mean speed or km-weighted v squared, and a first-drive-of-day / cold-start flag
payload for A1 = occupants only (luggage is assigned by class and is collinear with the class covariate)
update the counts to the M753 Rev 2.3 rule (609 with a pattern, 108 without)
state that the slope does not depend on the allowance A; the low / high payload bracket is a slope sensitivity
report the fuel-basis drive count (M768 step-basis caveat)
risks: occupants confounded with leisure, weekend and highway trips and HVAC
fuel mass 0 to 40 kg unobserved, same order as the payload SD
selection of the 108 drives without a pattern
regeneration limited by SOC and temperature
